sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:47250
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1392 of 2024

Applicant :- Khajan Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Mohammad Akram, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Amarnath Vishwakarma,
learned Brief Holder for the State-respondent.

2.  The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No.125 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 448, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali City,
District Bijnor, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 16.02.2023 against applicant by his brother and according to the FIR, applicant sold a house to the informant i.e. his brother but did not provide possession of the house.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that subsequently informant i.e. brother of the applicant came to know that over the property there was loan of the bank too.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of false allegation, the real brother of the applicant implicated the applicant in the present matter and applicant never committed any fraud.

entities.text: Khajan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that informant was well aware with the fact that there was a loan of the bank over the property but inspite of that he purchased house from the applicant.

He further submits,
applicant is ready to give the possession to him but he is not ready to take possession of the house.
6.
He further submits that even half of the loan amount of the bank has already been paid by the applicant.

7. He further submits that however applicant is having criminal history of three other cases but his criminal history has been explained in para 16 of the affidavit filed in support of the instant anticipatory bail application and in all cases applicant is on bail and except case under Section 376 I.P.C. other cases were of minor offences.
8. He further submits that investigation of the present case is still pending and police is trying to arrest the applicant.

9. Per contra, learned Brief Holder opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submit that applicant by playing fraud executed a sale-deed of the property in favour of the informant, who was his brother and he is also having criminal history of three other cases.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, as per allegation applicant even after execution of the sale-deed of the property did not give possession of the property to the informant, who is his real brother and also did not disclose the fact that he has also taken the loan over the property from the bank but argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that informant was well aware with the fact that there was a loan over the property cannot be ruled out.
12.

Further, however apart from the present case, applicant is having criminal history of three other cases but his criminal history has been explained in para 16 of the affidavit filed in support of the instant anticipatory bail application and in all cases applicant is on bail and except case under Section 376 I.P.C. other cases were of minor offences.

13. Further, considering the nature of allegation and the fact that all the alleged offneces are punishable with maximum punishment of seven years, custodial interrogation of the applicant does not appear to be necessary in the present matter.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: 17. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

18. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
